topic: Concurrency Design: Future Wait for Robust Synchronization
explanation: Futures provide a clean and robust method for inter-task synchronization. When a reacting task waits on a future corresponding to a `std::promise`, it is truly blocked and consumes no system resources while waiting. Crucially, this mechanism requires no explicit mutex management and is immune to spurious wakeups, a known hazard associated with condition variables.
practical_example: A main thread launches a worker task and needs to wait for the worker to finish initialization before proceeding. Using a future ensures the main thread blocks efficiently without polling or worrying about false signals inherent to condition variables.
chapter: Item 39: Consider void futures for one-shot event communication
book: Effective Modern C++ by Scott Meyers
